To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the knowledge of the surgical residents about the COVID 10 was low.

the knowledge of the surgical residents on COVID 19 is not adequate, the perception of the surgical residents about COVID 19 is positive, the motivation to work during this pandemic is high and the clinical behavior of the surgical residents in relation to COVID 19 is varied and individualized, and that a collective action is required to increase the compliance with the recommended practice guidelines.

Surgical residents' behavior in response to the COVID 19 outbreak was varied and individualized; despite demonstrating fair knowledge on the disease, less adherence to recommended clinical practice guidelines was noted; and high levels of stress were reported by surgical residents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent of adherence to practice guidelines among surgical residents and the factors associated with it.
the impact of the COVID 19 outbreak on surgical trainees in the Eastern Province and how they can cope with it.
the extent of association among surgical residents' clinical behaviors and their knowledge and perception about the COVID 10 disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the majority of surgical residents in the eastern province are not fully aware of the guidelines and recommendations for COVID 19, which could lead to increased risk of infection and spread of the disease.
the majority of surgical residents are not fully aware of the COVID 19 disease, and its associated guidelines.
there is a need for a more structured and comprehensive approach to the education of surgical residents in the management of COVID 19.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
surgical residents' knowledge, motivation, and perception of the COVID-19 are not associated with their behavior and clinical practices.
surgical residents' knowledge and practice are not in accordance with the recommended guidelines, and this is a cause of concern for the health care system.
the COVID 19 has affected the practice of surgery and surgical residents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the COVID 19 is a global challenge that needs a collective action to mitigate.
the COVID 19 has a huge effect on the surgical residents in Saudi Arabia.
the surgical residents' clinical practice and their adherence to the practice guidelines are highly variable and individualized.
